goal: The assistant acts without asking by default, and one toggle under the composer brings the approval card back.
scope: A. One policy at the single door every approval passes (main/providers/runs.js), asked each time so the toggle applies to a run in flight
B. A chip under the composer and a row in Settings › Assistant for the same app setting, approvals: none | ask
C. The browser's pauses on sensitive actions stay as they are, under their own setting
acceptance: By default no approval card appears and the action proceeds; choosing Ask first brings the card back, including in a run already in flight
A toggle under the composer and the same setting in Settings › Assistant
Delivered in a nightly from a green chain
nextAction: Picture cycle, chain and nightly for the approvals change; then the Windows terminal job on pull requests and C089's owner items.
truthReview: 2026-10-04: every approval (Claude Code's canUseTool for writes, commands, files outside the folder and unknown tools; the API loop's write_file; a goal worker's request relayed to main) goes through requestApproval in main/providers/runs.js. A policy handed in by the main process is asked each time: approvals other than 'ask' resolve at once with no card. Probed in the real app: default 'No approvals' resolves approved with zero cards; one click on the chip and the same request waits with one card; a second click and it resolves again. Unit test 3/3, journey 76/76. Not covered by a tour with a real provider run. Unchanged: Codex's own sandbox and approval policy (it never showed cards), the browser's pauses on sensitive actions, the rule that goal workers cannot start workers, the refusal to launch another browser.
screenshotReview: The composer shows the chip in both states and Settings › Assistant shows the row (probe frames reviewed); status shots and the visual run follow the implementation commit.
